name: How do you know if a garage is worth converting?

mainEntity.name: What signs tell you a garage is a good candidate for conversion instead of demolition and rebuilding?
mainEntity.text: What signs tell you a garage is a good candidate for conversion instead of demolition and rebuilding?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best garage conversion candidates share a few traits: the structure is sound, the ceiling height is workable, the slab is in usable condition, and utilities can be routed without excessive complexity. If those basics are in place, conversion often provides the best value because you are starting with an existing shell. The warning signs are equally important. Major settlement, severe roof issues, poor drainage, very low ceiling height, or a layout that cannot accommodate a functional room can push the project into rebuild territory. In those cases, the cost advantage of conversion shrinks fast. The decision should also reflect how the new room will be used. A simple office or guest room may fit well in a modest garage, while a full ADU may require more space and infrastructure than the structure can reasonably provide. A feasibility assessment should compare conversion cost against other options, including partial rebuild or addition. The right answer is not always to convert just because a garage exists. The right answer is the option that creates the best space with the least hidden risk and the highest long-term value.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage is worth converting when the structure is sound, the ceiling height works, the slab is serviceable, and utility routing is practical. If major structural repair, drainage correction, or extensive rebuilding is needed, a different addition strategy may be more cost-effective.
